content: {"summary":"On Sunday night the /var filesystem on kafka-03 exceeded 90% while the broker remained healthy. The on‑call team first ran `df -h /data/kafka` on all three brokers (RB‑009 step 1) and observed that kafka‑03’s partition disk usage was similar to its peers, so the partition volume was not the cause. Subsequent checks showed the root disk was filled by an unbounded systemd journal, which was cleared by vacuuming and limited with SystemMaxUse.","likely_cause":"Unbounded systemd journal growing on the root disk (/var) caused the >90% usage.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"Partition storage was ruled out because kafka‑03 was not an outlier on /data/kafka","evidence_ids":["INC-0149#0"],"quote":"Similar on each, kafka-03 not an outlier: partition storage cleared"},{"text":"The root disk fill was due to an unbounded systemd journal","evidence_ids":["INC-0149#1"],"quote":"Unbounded: nothing caps the journal here"},{"text":"Vacuuming the journal reduced /var usage below the alert threshold","evidence_ids":["INC-0149#1"],"quote":"Vacuum the journal to 500M"}],"next_checks":["Verify SystemMaxUse=500M persists after reboot","Add monitoring alert for journal size growth","Review RB‑009 runbook steps for future disk‑full incidents"]}
